title: Heirloom Tomato Bocconcini Sirloin Stacks
seoTitle: Heirloom Tomato Bocconcini Sirloin Stacks | Firehall BBQ
shortDescription: Caprese meets the grill—steak skewers with tomato and mozz for the hall
subtitle: Balsamic sirloin, cherry tomatoes, and fresh mozzarella for ten
description: Sirloin cubes marinate in balsamic and basil, grill with cherry tomatoes on skewers to 145°F, and finish with fresh mozzarella pearls and balsamic reduction.

steps.title: Marinate sirloin
steps.instruction: Toss beef cubes with balsamic, olive oil, basil, garlic, salt, and pepper. Marinate at least 1 hour refrigerated. Keep finished cold items below 41°F if they sit more than 30 minutes — nest the hotel pan on ice at the line. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early. Target 145°F for steaks, 160°F for ground at the thickest point before moving to the next batch.

steps.title: Reduce balsamic
steps.instruction: Simmer 0.25 cup balsamic until syrupy for drizzling. Cool. Reserve remaining balsamic for marinade. Maintain a steady simmer — bubbles should break the surface without a rolling boil that shreds delicate proteins. Plan about 10 minutes for this step at crew scale. Keep a backup tray at 200°F for firefighters returning from a call — never serve picked-over pans to late crew.

steps.title: Preheat grill grates
steps.instruction: Preheat grill to medium-high, 450°F. Oil grates. Plan about 8 minutes for this step at crew scale. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Thread caprese skewers
steps.instruction: Alternate beef cubes and cherry tomatoes on skewers. Leave small gaps for heat flow. Plan about 12 minutes for this step at crew scale. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early. Target 145°F for steaks, 160°F for ground at the thickest point before moving to the next batch.

steps.title: Grill skewers
steps.instruction: Grill 3–4 minutes per side until beef is charred and 140–145°F. Tomatoes should blister but stay intact. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Rest and hold
steps.instruction: Rest skewers 5 minutes. Slide beef and tomatoes into hotel pans, cover with foil, hold at 170°F. Hold covered at 140°F up to 20 minutes — log the time if your hall tracks food safety during long shifts. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early. Target 145°F for steaks, 160°F for ground at the thickest point before moving to the next batch.

steps.title: Caprese finish
steps.instruction: At the line, add mozzarella pearls and drizzle balsamic reduction. Do not add cheese before hold. Plan about 5 minutes for this step at crew scale. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Tonight's line
steps.instruction: Serve two skewers per firefighter with extra basil if available. Call temps: pull beef at 145°F. Plan about 5 minutes for this step at crew scale. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

proTips: Mozzarella at the line—heated cheese slides off skewers during hold.
Blistered tomatoes release juice; serve on platters with lips.
145°F pull with 5-minute rest hits perfect medium for sirloin cubes.
tonightSpread: Caprese steak skewers with mozzarella and balsamic.
Grilled bread brushed with olive oil.
leftovers: Chop into caprese steak salad with extra mozz.
Slice beef for steak bruschetta next shift.
whyCrewsLikeIt: Caprese steak skewers feel upscale but cook like any kebab. Beef holds at 170°F; mozzarella goes on cold at the line so it doesn't melt into a mess.
mealPrepNotes: Marinate beef 1–4 hours. Grill medium-high 450°F. Hold beef and tomatoes covered at 170°F up to 25 minutes. Mozzarella and balsamic at service only.
